subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should plain-text TUI rendering be activated by a persisted config key, automatic terminal detection, or an explicit TUI/CLI flag?
rationale: The prior PR selected a config key but was closed after deprioritization, while repository policy sets a high bar for new config and environment detection is imperfect; maintainer intent is needed for the durable public contract.

options.title: Explicit TUI flag
options.body: Add a documented `openclaw tui`/`openclaw chat` flag that avoids persistent config growth and provides a reliable user-controlled mode.

options.title: Persisted TUI setting
options.body: Add a strict `tui.accessibility` setting that persists across launches but enlarges config, schema, help, docs, and upgrade-sensitive surfaces.

options.title: Automatic detection
options.body: Infer the mode from terminal or accessibility environment signals, accepting false positives and negatives unless an explicit override is also added.

recommendation.title: Explicit TUI flag
recommendation.body: Add a documented `openclaw tui`/`openclaw chat` flag that avoids persistent config growth and provides a reliable user-controlled mode.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history and prior issue review connect steipete most strongly to the TUI architecture and product-level activation choice.
